nutshell: Nasdaq reverses lower on mixed Big Tech earnings.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: This is the closing bell briefing for February 3rd. The major indices were mixed today, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq notably finishing in the red.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Today's market can be summed up in one phrase: a Nasdaq reversal driven by mixed Big Tech earnings. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.34%, and the S&P 500 was also down 0.84%. The Nasdaq Composite saw the biggest drop among the major indices, falling 1.43%. On the other hand, the small-cap Russell 2000 index managed a slight gain, showing that the sell-off in large-cap tech didn't spread to the broader market. All eyes today were squarely on fourth-quarter corporate earnings reports.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So you're saying it was a day of starkly different fortunes depending on earnings. Which specific companies moved the market today?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, the prime examples were data analytics firm Palantir and payment services company PayPal. Palantir's stock surged over 6.8% after it reported better-than-expected earnings and a positive outlook, fueled by strong demand for its AI platform. But PayPal plunged more than 20% after announcing a weaker-than-expected profit forecast for the year, compounded by news of a CEO change. Ultimately, the shock from PayPal's poor performance overwhelmed Palantir's strong results, weighing on investor sentiment across the software and fintech sectors and leading the Nasdaq lower.

sources.title: Investors Love Palantir's Earnings. The Stock Is Soaring.
PayPal (NASDAQ:PYPL) Reports Sales Below Analyst Estimates In Q4 CY2025 Earnings, Stock Drops 14.6%

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see. So it was a day where the market reacted sensitively and moved in different directions based on individual company earnings. Could you summarize the key drivers for us today?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, the core story today was the mixed earnings reports from Big Tech and the subsequent weakness across the software sector. We'll break down these points one by one in just a moment.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, let's dive right into those details. You mentioned Palantir surging while PayPal plunged. Let's start with why the market's reaction was so sharply divided.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Right, today was a clear demonstration of how coldly investors are reacting to individual company report cards. While the S&P 500 closed down 0.84% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 1.43%, the story behind those numbers was the extreme divergence between Palantir and PayPal. Palantir jumped over 6.8% on excitement for its AI business, whereas PayPal plummeted more than 20% after issuing a disappointing forecast. This shockwave spread directly to related sectors; the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF dropped over 4.6%, and the Fintech ETF plunged more than 6%. Even though the December JOLTS report came in as expected and the 10-year Treasury yield remained stable, the negative fundamentals of a single company completely overshadowed the macroeconomic stability, freezing investor sentiment across the tech sector.

sources.title: JOLTS Job Openings

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I'm curious about the specific reasons the market was so enthusiastic about Palantir's earnings. What were the positive takeaways?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Palantir demonstrated explosive growth that blew past market expectations. Fourth-quarter revenue jumped 70% year-over-year to $1.41 billion, beating estimates. Growth in its U.S. business was particularly impressive, with government revenue up 66% and commercial revenue soaring by a staggering 137%. This proved that its AI platform, AIP, is moving beyond just a concept and is becoming an essential tool for real businesses and government agencies, translating into actual revenue. On top of that, the company provided guidance for the next quarter and the full year 2026 that also topped market forecasts, signaling strong confidence in its AI-driven growth story, which really drove investors to buy in.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: On the complete opposite end, PayPal's stock was in freefall. What part of its earnings report delivered such a shock to investors?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: PayPal's problem went beyond just missing Q4 estimates; it raised deep doubts about the company's future growth potential. While both Q4 revenue and adjusted EPS fell short of consensus, the real killer was the full-year 2026 forecast. The company projected that its profit would either slightly decline or see minimal growth, a stark contrast to Wall Street's expectation of about 8% growth. What was particularly damaging was the slowdown in its high-margin branded checkout business. To top it all off, the company announced it was abruptly replacing CEO Alex Chriss due to the poor performance, naming HP's Enrique Lores as the new chief. This added uncertainty from the leadership change, causing investor confidence to completely collapse.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So the impact of these two companies' results on the entire tech sector must have been significant.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Today's market sent a clear signal that it's starting to sharply distinguish between companies that can prove their AI story with actual results and those that can't. Palantir's success showed the commercial viability of AI technology, which had a positive spillover effect on its peers. But PayPal's failure amplified concerns across fintech and software in general. In fact, PayPal's stock plunge was a direct factor in the sharp drop of the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF, weighing down sentiment for the whole sector. This suggests that investors are no longer investing in tech stocks based on vague hopes; they're applying a very strict yardstick based on concrete earnings and growth outlooks.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Right, the PayPal shock seems to have had a major impact on the entire software sector. Could you break down for us how one company's earnings managed to sour sentiment for the whole sector?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, today was a day where the fall of a giant like PayPal cast a dark shadow over the entire tech space. While the Nasdaq fell 1.43%, the S&P 500 only dropped 0.84%, and both the 10-year Treasury yield and the Dollar Index were relatively stable. This clearly shows that today's shock wasn't a broad macroeconomic issue, but one confined to the tech sector, specifically software and fintech. And PayPal was at the epicenter. After its disappointing guidance, the stock plunged over 20%, dragging down related ETFs like the Global X Fintech ETF and the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF, which both fell over 5%. PayPal's weakness wasn't just seen as a company-specific problem; it raised fundamental questions about the growth prospects of the entire industry.

sources.title: Palantir Earnings Are 'A Warning to Peers' as Software Stocks Slump

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: A drop of over 20% is a massive shock. What exactly was in PayPal's report that caused such a severe market reaction?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: It wasn't just that Q4 revenue and EPS slightly missed estimates. What truly horrified investors was the outlook for the future. PayPal announced that its adjusted earnings for 2026 would either decline slightly or show almost no growth, a far cry from the roughly 8% growth Wall Street was expecting. The bigger problem was that growth in its core, high-margin branded payments business slowed dramatically, from 6% in the prior year's quarter to just 1% this quarter. On top of that, the news that the board had decided to abruptly replace the CEO, citing issues with his pace and execution, was taken as a signal of serious internal problems, triggering a massive sell-off.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So its core growth engine is sputtering and its leadership is shaky. But how did one company's problems spread to become a concern for the entire fintech and software sector?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Because PayPal is more than just a payments company; it acts as a bellwether for the health of online consumption and the digital economy. So when a company like PayPal posts weak results, citing a consumer slowdown and intense competition, investors grew anxious that other fintech firms like Block and Affirm would face similar headwinds. It was seen as a 'canary in the coal mine' warning. Furthermore, there's been a growing fear in the market of a 'SaaSpocalypse'—a Software-as-a-Service apocalypse—where the rise of AI could threaten the business models of existing software companies. PayPal's poor performance just poured fuel on that fire. In the end, the PayPal shock triggered two fears at once: a slowdown in the fintech industry and a structural crisis in the software industry.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: As you said, there was a lot of gloom in the software sector, but amid all that, Palantir showed a completely different picture and surged. What created that difference?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, it came down to the difference in 'tangible results' from AI. Palantir's stock jumped over 6.8% today, in stark contrast to PayPal. The company reported Q4 earnings that blew past expectations, with a particularly impressive 70% year-over-year revenue surge. The key driver for this growth was not only solid demand from government agencies but also a 137% explosion in its U.S. commercial revenue. This proved that Palantir's AI platform is being successfully adopted in real business settings, going beyond mere hype. Ultimately, today's market thoroughly separated and evaluated companies that are proving their growth by generating real profits from the AI megatrend, versus those facing increased competition and a slowdown in their traditional markets.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Okay, with the mixed fortunes in the software sector, the market's attention also turned to another tech giant: Nvidia. The stock closed down over 3% today. I'm curious about the reason behind that.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, Nvidia's drop today was triggered by an exclusive media report. News broke that a key customer, OpenAI, is unsatisfied with the performance of Nvidia's chips for certain inference tasks and is looking for alternatives. This sparked concerns about Nvidia's seemingly solid monopoly. It was seen as a sign that a risk the market had only considered potential could become a reality. This was particularly impactful because, according to its recent 10-Q filing, Nvidia has a very high customer concentration, with just four customers accounting for 61% of its total revenue. The possibility of its most iconic customer looking elsewhere dealt a significant blow to investor sentiment.

sources.title: Exclusive: OpenAI is unsatisfied with some Nvidia chips and looking for alternatives, sources say

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: News about a key customer's dissatisfaction... that's bound to have a big impact. But doesn't Nvidia have the powerful CUDA software ecosystem? It can't be easy for customers to find an alternative.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's a very sharp point. However, it's crucial to note that the core of this issue isn't the 'training' market, where AI models are developed, but the 'inference' market, where finished models are applied to services. The powerful lock-in effect of the CUDA ecosystem is absolute in the training market, but analysts say its influence is relatively weaker in the inference market. In an inference environment, cost-efficiency and fast response times are more critical, creating a greater incentive to adopt competitor chips or in-house chips optimized for specific tasks. Therefore, OpenAI's move could be interpreted as the first sign of a crack in Nvidia's monopoly, suggesting its dominance might not be as solid in inference, the next major battleground in the AI market.

sources.title: Exclusive: OpenAI is unsatisfied with some Nvidia chips and looking for alternatives, sources say

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see, so as the market's center of gravity shifts, a new competitive landscape could emerge. But isn't there also a view that sees this as an opportunity, not a crisis?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, absolutely. From a positive perspective, this incident is seen as 'growing pains' on the path to a larger market. The demands of a highly sophisticated customer like OpenAI can actually provide a clear roadmap for Nvidia's next-generation architecture development. Also, CEO Jensen Huang's own mention of potentially investing in an OpenAI IPO could be seen not as a defensive move to prevent a customer from leaving, but as an aggressive expansion strategy to share a technology roadmap and solidify the ecosystem with a key partner. There's also a persuasive argument that while competitors are competing on individual chip performance, Nvidia is changing the game by competing as an integrated platform that encompasses hardware, software, and networking.

sources.title: Nvidia will consider investing in OpenAI IPO, CEO Huang tells CNBC

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So we have two competing narratives: the pessimistic view that this is the first crack in the monopoly, and the optimistic view that it's just a growing pain on the way to bigger things. It must be difficult for investors to know what to think.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. The bottom line is that while Nvidia's long-term growth potential remains intact, the uncertainty has clearly increased as the theoretical threats of customer concentration risk and intensifying competition have started to become reality. The bull case for its platform is strong, but the bear case—the structural threat of 'your customer is also your competitor'—is also a reality that can't be ignored. Therefore, at this point, rather than taking an aggressive position, it seems a more cautious approach is warranted, watching the moves of other major customers and waiting to see if Nvidia's next-generation products can effectively address the concerns in the inference market.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Okay, let's recap today's market action. With concerns about Fed rate hikes continuing, the market seemed a bit unsettled.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. The market today saw increased volatility as the pressure from the Fed's tightening stance intersected with mixed corporate earnings. The tech-heavy Nasdaq saw a relatively larger pullback, reflecting the weakness in growth stocks, which are more sensitive to rising interest rates. For the time being, investors will have to keep a close eye on every macroeconomic data point, alongside individual company fundamentals.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So, for the rest of the week, what are the key economic indicators that investors should be watching?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: This week is packed with indicators that will give us a read on the health of the labor market. First up, on Wednesday local time—that's tomorrow—we'll get the ADP employment report, which shows private-sector hiring, and the ISM Services PMI, which gauges the services economy. Both of these will be closely watched as they are important previews for the official Labor Department jobs report on Friday.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: As you mentioned, the jobs report on Friday seems to be the most important one. What specifically should we be looking for?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, it's definitely the highlight of the week. We need to watch all three key components: non-farm payrolls, the unemployment rate, and average hourly earnings. The market's preferred scenario would be a slowdown in new job creation while the unemployment rate remains stable, and most importantly, a deceleration in wage growth. If wage pressures remain high, it could fuel concerns that the Fed will have to stay tighter for longer, which would weigh on the market. So it's about assessing the quantity and quality of jobs, as well as wage inflation pressures, all together.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it all comes back to the Fed's policy decisions. Finally, do you have any closing thoughts for our investors?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, for the time being, the market is likely to react strongly to each economic data release. This week's jobs report and next week's scheduled CPI release will be critical turning points for the market's short-term direction. Therefore, it's a time when investors need to try to read the bigger market trends with a long-term perspective, rather than being swayed by short-term volatility. It's more important than ever to carefully examine the earnings and growth potential of individual companies.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Thank you for your detailed analysis today. That was the U.S. market closing bell briefing for February 3rd. Thanks for listening.
